rationale: B wins because it keeps four usable routes closer to the supplied facts: "Allbirds adds a wholesale partner as it pulls back from its own stores" is a clean channel story with the missing proof named. A is sharper in places, but "A DTC pioneer that spent a decade avoiding wholesale" invents a decade-long posture the update never gave it; that is how a smart pitch gets killed in paragraph one. B still has to clean up "starts to bite" and the stock-picking odor, but it gives the founder safer raw material.
gaps_in_A: "A DTC pioneer that spent a decade avoiding wholesale" smuggles in history not supplied. The update only says a named wholesale partnership is part of the relaunch.
"That's a company publicly conceding its signature product had a durability problem" overstates "more durable than its original wool runner" into an admission of defect.
"the company is arguing against a position it helped popularize" imports a sustainability-history thesis absent from the update. Source it or cut it.
The sustainability durability angle partly duplicates the material durability angle, and the set admits "these collapse into one" if the executive will not make the argument.
gaps_in_B: "funding-mechanics" is the wrong label for a public-company turnaround/earnings angle. It smells like a template field that wandered into the room.
"starts to bite" and "comeback" dress one quarter of gross-margin improvement as momentum while the company remains net-loss-making and below IPO price.
"buy signal or a value trap" pushes toward stock-picking territory. A company pitch should be careful not to invite a markets reporter to write a valuation call.
"durability is the chronic knock against natural-material shoes" may be true, but it is not in the supplied facts. Bring evidence or leave it out.
